prompt.purpose: Write a merge request description from the change-set below and, when present, the vulnerability-set. The description tells a reviewer what the change is and why the code looks the way it does; it is not a record of how the work went. Match the structure of the example: a numbered Change Summary grouped by behavior, then a Security Analysis section.

instructions.always: Describe only what the diff and the vulnerability comparison show, and tie each point to a specific code change or finding. Group changes by behavior, not by file.
Describe code as new or added only when the diff creates it; code in unchanged context lines, or that was renamed, moved, or modified, already existed.

In Security Analysis, state new vulnerabilities and their impact, acknowledge fixed ones, and say plainly when nothing changed. When no vulnerability-set is provided, write "No vulnerability data provided".

Describe the result, not the work: leave out process narration (addressing review feedback, fixing an earlier commit on the branch), follow-up lists, test-plan checklists, and restatements of what the diff already shows.

Plain engineer vocabulary, roughly 150 to 350 words. Avoid filler and grading words: "worth noting", "notably", "leverage", "robust", "seamless", "comprehensive", "holistic", "delve", "ensure" (say "make sure"), "honest", "principled", "proper", "clean", and calling a check a "signal". Punctuate with commas, colons, periods, or parentheses; no em-dashes or en-dashes.

End the response with the last concrete change or finding. The reader wants facts, so leave out closing summaries, value judgments ("a significant improvement"), and predictions about future benefits.

prompt.example:
Change Summary:
1. **Session handling** - Add JWT middleware that validates the bearer token on every /api route - Add login and register endpoints; tokens expire after 24 hours because the refresh flow is not in this change
2. **Dependency updates** - Update bcrypt from 5.0.1 to 5.1.1 - Replace the deprecated createCipher calls with createCipheriv
Security Analysis: - No new vulnerabilities introduced - The two medium severity bcrypt findings are resolved by the 5.1.1 upgrade
